content: Leaf spot commonly appears as brown or black circular spots on leaves. It spreads faster in humid weather and crowded planting conditions. Farmers should remove highly infected leaves, avoid overhead irrigation, improve spacing, and consult a local agriculture officer before chemical treatment.

Leaf blight causes yellowing, browning, and drying of leaf areas. It can reduce crop yield if not managed early. Farmers should remove affected plant material, avoid excess moisture, use disease-free seeds, and seek expert guidance before applying fungicide.
The leaf appears healthy. Farmers should continue regular monitoring, balanced irrigation, proper sunlight exposure, and nutrient management. Early observation helps prevent disease spread.

For leaf spot prevention, maintain field hygiene, remove fallen infected leaves, rotate crops where possible, and avoid watering leaves directly. Use chemical treatment only after local expert recommendation.

Leaf blight management includes early detection, pruning infected areas, improving airflow, and using resistant crop varieties when available. Severe cases should be checked by an agricultural extension officer.
